note: Paper test of POSTING resting orders on Kalshi game-winner contracts instead of taking prices (research: reports/NFL and college betting edges.md, rank 2: maker fee 0.0175*p*(1-p) vs taker 0.07*p*(1-p); on Kalshi makers lost far less than takers; exchanges don't limit winners). Simulated, nothing is posted. Each hourly run posts one hypothetical 1-contract YES bid per team at (Pinnacle Shin fair - margin), only when that bid would be the new best bid and below the best ask (a maker, not a taker). The order lives until the next run or 30 min before kickoff. Fill = a trade in that window printed strictly BELOW our bid (the price traded through us, so a resting order there was certainly filled); 'touch' fills (trade at our price) are logged but not graded, since queue position is unknown. The real risk is adverse selection: we get filled when the price is moving against us. Graded by CLV vs Pinnacle's Shin close and by results.
